title: Hangul
prompt: Listen. Which consonant do you hear? (It is played together with ㅏ.)

questions.note: You heard 가 = ㄱ + ㅏ. ㄱ sounds somewhere between g and k.
You heard 나 = ㄴ + ㅏ. ㄴ sounds like the n in "no".
You heard 다 = ㄷ + ㅏ. ㄷ sounds somewhere between d and t.
You heard 라 = ㄹ + ㅏ. ㄹ sounds like a soft r between vowels and like l at the end of a syllable.
You heard 마 = ㅁ + ㅏ. ㅁ sounds like the m in "mom".
You heard 바 = ㅂ + ㅏ. ㅂ sounds somewhere between b and p.
You heard 사 = ㅅ + ㅏ. ㅅ sounds like s. Before ㅣ (i) it sounds more like sh, as in 시 (si).

questions.prompt: Listen. Which vowel do you hear?
questions.note: You heard 아 = ㅇ + ㅏ. ㅇ is silent at the start of a syllable, so you only hear the vowel. ㅏ sounds like the a in "father".

questions.prompt: Listen. Which vowel do you hear?
questions.note: You heard 어 = ㅇ + ㅓ. ㅓ sounds like the o in "son".

questions.prompt: Listen. Which vowel do you hear?
questions.note: You heard 오 = ㅇ + ㅗ. ㅗ sounds like the o in "go", but shorter.
